question.problem: Mark runs a hotel near a popular tourist resort. He knows that, on average, people usually book their room $3.5$ days before their trip. By modeling the number of days between the customer's booking and arrival as continuous and assuming that these numbers are independent, determine the probability that the next customer books their room less than $1$ full day in advance. Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Since the time interval between the customer's booking and arrival is continuous and the time of different bookings are independent and occur at a constant average rate, we can model the time between the next customer's booking and arrival using an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of days between a booking and the customer's arrival. Since customers book their room $3.5=7/2$ days in advance on average, $X$ can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda =2/7,$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{2}{7}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{7}{e}^{-2x/7}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a customer books a room less than $1$ full day in advance is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2}{7}{e}^{-2x/7}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-2x/7}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-{e}^{-2/7}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.2485\end{aligned}
$$
